faults.note: Screen 10 and the explanation say each sloping bar's up part holds half the load without saying why: the two bars slope equally, so they share it equally. The explanation says the bottom bar pulls the feet together but not why it must: the roller cannot push sideways. And it never says why joint by joint is enough. The count itself is the reason: j joints give 2j balance equations, and a simple frame's m bars and three support pushes are m + 3 = 2j unknowns. Add that one sentence, which ties the two halves of the lesson together.

'The supports take away three more' ties 2j − 3 to a pin and a roller; two pinned feet take away four, so the count would read differently. Recast it as true of the frame alone: three of the 2j ways to move are the whole frame sliding and turning, which do not change its shape, so holding its shape needs at least 2j − 3 bars whatever it stands on. The supports then stop those three. Screens 3, 4 and 5 and whatAmILookingAt follow. 'The roller only pushes straight up' holds for a roller on level ground; say so in the practice's mistake. 'Real screws lose much of the push to friction' is vague; 'a good part' is safer. The analogy's 'with as many equations as unknowns, every unknown comes out' needs the equations to be independent; soften to 'enough equations'.
